A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CRSA research. Their complete text, equations, tables, figures, and Appendices A–D are readable and support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original 500-round reference-game simulations and an evaluation on 65 MDDial samples, including numerical results and belief visualizations.

after.justification: v2 retains the original reference-game results and reports perplexity and diagnostic task success on 1,878 MDDial samples.

M1.justification: The proposed YRSA/CRSA gain functions, history-dependent belief factors, alternating updates, and LLM speaker interface are retained. The medical prompting and comparator revisions do not introduce a new CRSA algorithm component.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same card-reference task and template-based MDDial diagnosis task. The larger medical sample and revised prompt examples change settings within existing coverage.

E2.justification: Section 6 revises the reported Literal diagnostic comparator: v1 scores candidate disease substitutions in the final utterance, whereas v2 constructs the literal listener using Equation (7), with the LLM speaker as lexicon. Comparator names and the reference-game comparison methods remain unchanged.

E3.justification: The medical evaluation changes from 65 samples with an unspecified split to 1,878 training-split samples, replacing speaker/listener entropy with speaker perplexity and diagnostic task success. Appendix C also replaces the few-shot conversations and symptom lists. These substantially revise the reported evaluation protocol.

E4.justification: The history-dependent lexicon comparisons, qualitative alpha-sensitivity observations, and Figure 3 belief-tracking example are retained. Appendix D already provides the reference-game dispersion analysis in v1; v2 adds no distinct ablation or robustness experiment.

E5.justification: Both versions include standard-deviation error bars for the reference-game results in Appendix D, Figure 4. No new seeds, repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, or significance tests are reported; both medical tables provide point estimates.

E6.justification: Table 1 replaces entropy pairs of 8.18/2.19, 14.27/2.86, and 18.00/3.29 for CRSA, RSA, and Literal with perplexity/success pairs of 15.362/0.085, 15.395/0.085, and 60.835/0.079. The revised medical results show nearly equal CRSA/RSA performance. Changed metrics, samples, and settings prevent interpreting these as same-setting performance changes. Reference-game results are retained.

T1.justification: The formal RSA/YRSA/CRSA objectives, fixed-prior assumptions, update equations, complexity statements, and derivations in Appendices A–B are substantively unchanged. Notation clarifications and the revised empirical metrics do not add a theoretical result.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same central claims about information-theoretic multi-turn reasoning, private-belief tracking, shared tasks, and collaborative behavior. The added introductory overview restates these contributions.

C2.justification: Section 6 replaces the strong medical entropy-advantage interpretation with a qualified account of nearly equal RSA/CRSA performance. It attributes this to nearly uniform inferred patient beliefs, acknowledges low diagnostic success, and suggests stronger LLM initialization. The broader limitations and reference-game interpretations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v2 adds code-repository and checkpoint links and newly documents symptom–diagnosis counting for the prior and a singleton doctor meaning space. Appendix C revises the supplied prompts, while the explicit precomputation description from v1 is removed. These are localized reproducibility changes.

R1.justification: v2 adds citations to GLIMPSE by Darrin et al. (2024) and (RSA)² by Spinoso-Di Piano et al. (2025). It also refines the description of persona consistency and criticism of earlier methods, while retaining the broader research positioning.

P1.justification: v2 adds an introductory overview, reorganizes Section 6 under Methodology, Metrics, and Results, removes a subsection heading while retaining its content, and makes terminology and explanatory edits. The main narrative order and most prose remain intact.

P2.justification: Figure 1 is redrawn, Figures 2 and 3 are placed together, and Figure 4 moves to a separate page. Table 1 receives revised metric headings and a wider layout. All four figures are retained, with unchanged reference-game plots.

improvement.justification: The added prior-construction and code-access information improves reproducibility, while the medical discussion more candidly acknowledges near-tied RSA/CRSA performance and low diagnostic success. These are modest gains in transparency. Important weaknesses remain: the broad effectiveness claims are retained, and the new success-rate formula has a negative sign inconsistent with the positive values in Table 1.
